description: Extract a design system (colors, typography, components, spacing, dark mode if shown) by looking at reference UI screenshots, not by guessing from a description. If the user lacks a PRD, help build a minimal one first (pitch, problem, audience, must-haves), then compose the design system and PRD into one implementation-ready prompt for a UI-generation step. Use when the user provides UI screenshots/mockups and wants a design system extracted, wants to match (not copy) an app's look, wants tokens pulled from visual examples, wants an MVP PRD before UI work, or wants implementation-ready UI prompts from references plus a rough idea. Use even without "design system" — "pull the palette from these screenshots," "match this app's vibe," "turn these mockups into a style guide." Not for auditing a built UI for bugs, generating style directions with no references, or writing implementation code once the prompt exists.

results.query: Extract a design system from these reference UI screenshots for my new app.
I have mockups I like the look of — pull out the color palette, typography, and spacing into documentation.
Build an MVP UI that matches the aesthetic of these reference screenshots.
Generate implementation-ready UI prompts based on this design system and my product idea.
I don't have a PRD yet, but I have reference images — help me build both before generating UI prompts.
These screenshots are dark mode — extract the design tokens including dark mode variants.
Create consistent UI variations for my app following the design language in these references.
Turn these competitor app screenshots into a reusable design system doc for our team.
Audit this already-built page for visual bugs and layout defects.
Generate multiple different visual style directions since I can't describe what I want.
Write the actual React components implementing this existing design spec.
Explain the difference between a design system and a component library.
Create a QA test plan for this application.
Fix the layout overflow bug on this page's mobile view.
Write a product requirements document for a new feature, no design work needed.
Compress and optimize these image files for faster page load.
